attested.notes: Second round of the same pass, run against the canonical voice engine doc rather than the stage pack alone. Three of its rules were under-delivered first time round. Rule C (a lived-reality anchor in every major section) failed in four sections: Compare Your Closure Options, The Pre-Closure Checklist, When Can You Become Personally Liable, and the cost section. Each now carries one drawn from practice, not invention: which of the six positions the director is actually in being the unsettled question, the two checklist steps nobody chases you for, guarantees and loan accounts being what actually costs directors money while conduct claims are what they fear, and the funding column deciding options as much as the route does. The doc's enforcement rule 'zero you in any section longer than 200 words means that section is not serving the reader' failed in the cost and timescale sections, which had literally no you or your across 275 and 266 words; article_audit check 27 passed both, so this is a gap the mechanical gate does not see. Both now translate to reader consequence: who the fee falls to when the company cannot fund a CVL, and the appointment being the date that matters because that is when creditor letters stop arriving at your address. Rule J (the ending compresses the real decision and states what is left unsolved) failed: the page ended on a four-step action list. It now closes by naming what closing does and does not achieve, including that no practitioner, ourselves included, can make a guarantee or a loan account balance disappear. Variation moves added per the rhythm section: one rhetorical question that mirrors the reader's real question ('So will anyone actually chase it?') and one earned attitude transition. Rule H institutional we strengthened by surfacing verification labour that was previously confined to the disclosure box: we went to the Insolvency Service's own MVL review rather than trade averages. HONEST SHORTFALL, recorded rather than papered over: the doc's pronoun table targets we/our at 10-15 per 1,000 words. The page is at 7.6, up from 6.1. The floor of 5 is comfortably met and every instance shows method, caseload or judgement, but the target is not met. Padding to reach it would breach Rule H and the stage pack's explicit ban on hollow we, so it is left short and reported. Rule B checked for floating evaluative labels: none (the only hit was 'bond premium', a technical term). Stranger-read report is the same one, and remains valid: this round did not change the opening it reviewed. Its one open point also stands, that the page gives no practitioner fee figure to decide on.
